route_note: Take the R5 Rodalies commuter train from Barcelona to Monistrol de Montserrat, then the Cremallera rack railway (or the Aeri cable car from Monistrol-Vila) up to the monastery.
see: Montserrat Benedictine Monastery and the Basilica of Our Lady of Montserrat
The Black Madonna (La Moreneta) in the basilica
Montserrat Boys' Choir (Escolania), when performing
Sant Jeroni viewpoint hike
Santa Cova pilgrimage path

route_note: Take the R2 Sud Rodalies train from Barcelona-Sants or Passeig de Gràcia directly to Sitges, about 40 minutes, then walk to the beach and old town.
see: Old town (Vila) and its whitewashed streets
Church of Sant Bartomeu i Santa Tecla on the seafront
Playa de la Ribera and Playa de Sant Sebastià
Museu Romàntic
Carnival and Film Festival atmosphere, seasonal

route_note: Take a high-speed AVE or Rodalies regional train from Barcelona-Sants or Passeig de Gràcia to Girona, about 40 to 90 minutes depending on service; the old town is a short walk from the station.
see: Girona Cathedral and its long Gothic nave
Call (Jewish Quarter) and Museu d'Història dels Jueus
Colourful houses along the Onyar River
City walls and Passeig de la Muralla
Game of Thrones filming locations

route_note: Take a regional train (R14 Rodalies or regional service) from Barcelona-Sants to Tarragona, about 1 to 1.5 hours; the Roman sites are a short walk or bus ride from the station.
see: Roman Amphitheatre by the sea
Roman Circus and Passeig Arqueològic
Tarragona Cathedral
Medieval old town and Part Alta
Museu Nacional Arqueològic de Tarragona

route_note: Take a high-speed AVE or regional train from Barcelona-Sants or Passeig de Gràcia to Figueres-Vilafant or Figueres, about 1 to 1.5 hours; the Dalí museum is a short walk from the station.
see: Dalí Theatre-Museum
Castell de Sant Ferran
Dalí Jewels Museum
Rambla and old town of Figueres
Dalí's birthplace and Plaça del Gala
